Early Picks & Predictions for Colts vs Texans (TNF)

By Michael Harrison in NFL News

Published: November 16, 2026 at 8:48 pm EST

  • The 3-7 Colts square off against the 3-6 Texans to kick off Week 11 on Thursday Night Football
  • Houston has won six of eight vs the Colts but lost to them in Week 3
  • See the early lines for TNF Indianapolis vs Houston and picks
Listen to audio version of this article

Instaread

The Houston Texans (3-6 SU, 3-6 ATS, 6-3 O/U) cling to a 26.5% chance to reach the playoffs as they host the Indianapolis Colts (3-7 SU, 5-5 ATS, 6-4 O/U) in an AFC South showdown. Indianapolis arrives off a recent victory but finds itself essentially eliminated from postseason contention with just a 0.7% playoff probability. This divisional clash kicks off at 8:15 PM ET / 5:15 PM PT Thursday Night at Reliant Stadium in Houston, with the broadcast streaming on Amazon Prime Video and TSN.

Below, I will break down the opening lines and find the best Colts/Texans picks to target early in the week before the odds shift.

Colts vs Texans Opening Betting Lines

Odds as of Monday, November 16 at BetMGM. Sign up and place your wagers at BetMGM.

The Texans hold an 82.6% implied probability of winning outright. The Colts sit at just a 17.4% chance. For bettors playing the moneyline, a $10 wager on the heavily favored Texans yields a total payout of only $11.60 (a $1.60 profit). That same $10 flyer on the underdog Colts returns a massive $55.00 payout ($45.00 profit) if they orchestrate a road upset.

Checking the latest NFL odds reveals significant line movement since the opener. Heavy action steamed the consensus opening spread of Houston -5.5 all the way out to -11.

Early Picks for Colts vs Texans on TNF

Spread Pick: Houston Texans -10.5 (-108 / 52¢, Kalshi)

The underlying seasonal statistics point heavily toward the Texans covering the massive 11-point spread. The Texans boast a high-scoring offense averaging 25.9 points and 349.1 total yards per game.

In contrast, the Indianapolis offense manages just 20.8 points and 287.6 yards per contest. Houston has produced at a consistent clip despite a 3-6 record, with C.J. Stroud executing efficiently behind an offensive line that has allowed just 17 sacks across nine games (1.9 per contest).

Indianapolis’ offensive production continues to lag, surrendering 27.1 points per game defensively while yielding 26 sacks offensively, creating severe play-script disadvantages against high-end defensive fronts.

The biggest mismatch in this game comes down to ball security and pressure rate. Indianapolis enters the matchup with a concerning -12 turnover differential. They will be lining up against a Houston defense that has already racked up 33 total sacks on the season and maintains a positive turnover differential of +4 (yielding just five giveaways against nine takeaways).

Over/Under Pick: Over 44.5 (+100, Novig)

Taking the Over presents the most logical play for the game total. Houston converts red zone trips into touchdowns at a stellar 65.6% rate. The Colts’ 61.5% red zone efficiency is also highly respectable. With Houston’s potent offense likely capitalizing on short fields generated by the Colts’ turnover issues, I expect this affair to surpass the total. Over bettors have cashed routinely on both sides this season, with Houston going 6-3 to the over and Indianapolis standing at 6-4 to the over.

Indianapolis’ defense has surrendered 27.1 points per game and allowed opponents to clear 27 points in four of their last five outings. When combined with Stroud’s ability to finish inside the 20 and the Colts’ knack for quick-strike scoring or costly turnovers that flip field position in seconds, this total is set several points too low.

Player Prop Pick: Nico Collins Anytime TD (+127 / 44¢, Kalshi)

For a high-upside play, I am targeting Nico Collins in the Anytime Touchdown market. Buying a Collins TD contract at 44¢ on Kalshi (equal to +127 odds) provides excellent value.

He draws an ideal matchup against an Indianapolis secondary bleeding 8.0 yards per passing attempt. Collins has already found paydirt five times across seven appearances on the campaign, including back-to-back scoring performances in Weeks 9 and 10 against the Chargers and Browns. Stroud targeted Collins an astounding 16 times last week alone, cementing his status as Houston’s undisputed top red-zone read.

Against a Colts pass defense that has conceded 18 passing touchdowns and struggles to match up with big-bodied boundary receivers, Collins offers premier touchdown equity.

IND vs HOU Team Stats

The most glaring mismatch in this tilt is the Texans’ potent aerial assault facing a vulnerable Colts pass defense. C.J. Stroud (O/U 256.5 passing yards) should have plenty of opportunities to find Nico Collins down the field against a secondary consistently failing to limit explosive plays.

On the other side, Daniel Jones (O/U 183.5 passing yards) will be forced into rushed decisions by a Houston pass rush that feasts on turnover-prone signal-callers. For more insights, check out sports betting picks.
